edges.description: Somatic IDH1/2 driver mutation in glial-lineage precursor cells defines IDH-mutant diffuse glioma subtypes.

edges.description: Transformed cells infiltrate brain parenchyma along white-matter tracts.

Telomerase reactivation confers replicative immortality that sustains continued tumor-cell proliferation and growth.

edges.description: Cortical and subcortical parenchymal infiltration and peritumoral microenvironmental disruption provoke glioma-related seizures.
Parenchymal tumor expansion and peritumoral vasogenic edema elevate intracranial pressure, causing headache.
Diffuse infiltration across white-matter tracts and eloquent association networks impairs cognition.
Infiltration and mass effect involving dominant-hemisphere language cortices and white-matter pathways produce aphasia.
Infiltration or compression of corticospinal motor cortex and white-matter tracts causes focal muscle weakness.
Brainstem or corticobulbar pathway involvement and mass effect impair swallowing.
Parenchymal tumor burden, mass effect, and peritumoral edema contribute to prominent clinical fatigue.

nodes.description: Glioma types are defined in part by large-scale chromosomal copy-number alterations: combined whole chromosome 7 gain and chromosome 10 loss (+7/-10) and CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma; whole-arm 1p/19q codeletion in oligodendroglioma; and CDKN2A/B loss upgrading IDH-mutant astrocytoma to grade 4. These reflect underlying chromosomal instability.

nodes.description: IDH1 or IDH2 mutation is the primary biological divider of adult-type diffuse glioma. Mutant IDH acquires neomorphic activity producing the oncometabolite D-2-hydroxyglutarate, which competitively inhibits alpha-ketoglutarate-dependent dioxygenases (TET DNA demethylases and histone demethylases), yielding a glioma CpG-island methylator phenotype and a block in glial differentiation. IDH-mutant tumors carry a more favorable prognosis than IDH-wildtype.

evidence.reference_title: Vorasidenib in IDH1- or IDH2-Mutant Low-Grade Glioma.
evidence.snippet: Progression-free survival was significantly improved in the vorasidenib group as compared with the placebo group (median progression-free survival, 27.7 months vs. 11.1 months; hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.39; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.27 to 0.56; P<0.001).
